metadataReview.note: Reviewed location: Rangiriri site S13/50, the Māori defensive works attacked on 20–21 November 1863. The marker uses the archaeological inventory reference, whose rounding and southwest-corner convention are retained; no new metric error radius is claimed. The wider defensive line and later Te Wheoro redoubt are not reduced to this point. Dates remain unchanged.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: DOC p.42 gives Rangiriri archaeological site S13/50 at NZMS 260/NZMG 2698700E 6417200N. Transforming EPSG:27200 to EPSG:4326 gives longitude 175.1291245061598, latitude -37.427638341033614; atlas point rounded to three decimals. DOC p.15 states references are rounded to 50/100 metres and generally locate the southwest site corner. This is an archaeological-site reference, not a battlefield centroid or individual tactical position.
